Apple___Apple_scab.remedy: Prune and remove infected leaves and fruit. Apply a fungicide (e.g., products containing myclobutanil or copper) early in the season and at green tip. Avoid overhead irrigation.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, ensure good airflow (prune canopy), and practice sanitation by removing fallen leaves/fruit.

Apple___Black_rot.remedy: Remove and destroy infected branches and mummified fruit. Apply appropriate fungicide sprays during the growing season when infections are active.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Sanitation and pruning to improve air circulation; avoid leaving infected debris in orchard.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.remedy: Prune out heavily infected branches and remove nearby cedar/juniper hosts if possible. Apply protective fungicides during the period when spores are active.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Avoid planting susceptible apple varieties near cedar/juniper hosts; choose resistant cultivars and practice pruning for airflow.

Apple___healthy.remedy: No treatment needed. Continue routine cultural practices: irrigation management, balanced fertilization, and monitoring for pests/diseases.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Monitor regularly for early symptoms; maintain good orchard sanitation and proper pruning.

Blueberry___healthy.remedy: No treatment needed. Maintain soil pH, adequate irrigation and mulching.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Monitor for pests/diseases and follow good cultural practices.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.remedy: No treatment needed. Keep orchard clean and monitor for diseases and pests.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Proper pruning, sanitation, and irrigation management.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.remedy: Remove and destroy infected shoots. Apply fungicides labeled for powdery mildew on stone fruit during active growth.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Improve air circulation, avoid overhead watering, and apply sulphur or other preventative treatments if recommended locally.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.remedy: Remove and destroy infected crop residues. Use fungicide sprays if disease pressure is high and growth stage is susceptible.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Rotate crops, use resistant hybrids, and use residue management (tillage or removal).

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust.remedy: If infections are severe, apply recommended fungicides at appropriate growth stages.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, and rotate crops. Monitor weather and treat when conditions favor rust.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.remedy: Remove or disk infected debris. Fungicide applications may be needed under heavy disease pressure.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Use resistant hybrids and crop rotation; avoid continuous corn planting.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.remedy: No treatment; follow best agronomy practices.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Regular scouting and maintain crop rotation and variety selection.

Grape___Black_rot.remedy: Remove infected clusters and mummified fruit, prune affected shoots. Apply fungicides during bloom and pre-bunch closure if needed.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Sanitation and pruning to improve airflow, use resistant varieties when available.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).remedy: Remove and destroy severely infected wood; there are limited chemical controls and management focuses on removal of affected vines.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid wounding vines, maintain vine vigor, and remove infected material promptly.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.remedy: Apply fungicides if disease pressure is significant and remove infected leaves to reduce inoculum.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Improve canopy ventilation and apply regular sprays during wet periods if recommended locally.

Grape___healthy.remedy: No treatment; continue standard vineyard care.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).remedy: There is no cure. Remove and destroy infected trees to prevent spread. Control the vector (Asian citrus psyllid) with insecticides where appropriate.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material, monitor and control psyllid populations, and follow local integrated pest management (IPM) guidelines.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.remedy: Prune out heavily infected areas and apply copper-based sprays as permitted for stone fruit during active infection periods.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use clean nursery stock, improve air flow by pruning, and avoid overhead irrigation during wet conditions.

Peach___healthy.remedy: No treatment needed. Keep trees pruned and monitor.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.remedy: Remove infected plants/fruit and use copper sprays where allowed. Avoid handling plants when wet to reduce spread.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified seed/seedlings and practice crop rotation and sanitation.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.remedy: No treatment; maintain proper watering and nutrition.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Monitor for pests and diseases regularly.

Potato___Early_blight.remedy: Remove and destroy infected foliage; apply appropriate fungicides (e.g., chlorothalonil or mancozeb) according to label instructions.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, avoid overhead watering, and use certified seed potatoes.

Potato___Late_blight.remedy: Remove infected plants immediately. Apply effective fungicides quickly when conditions are favorable for late blight and follow local advisories.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties if available, rotate crops, and maintain good drainage.

Potato___healthy.remedy: No treatment; maintain good cultural practices.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Use certified seed and monitor for signs of disease, especially in wet conditions.

Raspberry___healthy.remedy: No treatment. Provide proper pruning and sanitation.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Monitor for common pests and rotate plantings if possible.

Soybean___healthy.remedy: No treatment; follow recommended soybean agronomy.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Use certified seed, rotate crops and scout regularly.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.remedy: Remove and destroy infected leaves and apply fungicides labeled for powdery mildew on cucurbits.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, ensure good airflow, and avoid high humidity around the plants.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.remedy: Remove and discard infected leaves. Improve air circulation and apply fungicides as recommended for strawberry leaf scorch.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Maintain good spacing of plants, proper irrigation management, and use disease-free runners.

Strawberry___healthy.remedy: No treatment; keep plants mulched and well watered.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Monitor for pests and disease; use certified runner plants.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.remedy: Remove infected plant debris and apply copper-based bactericides if allowed. Avoid handling plants when wet.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified seed, rotate crops and practice good sanitation.

Tomato___Early_blight.remedy: Remove affected foliage, apply recommended fungicides, and rotate crops.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties and avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Late_blight.remedy: Remove infected plants immediately; use appropriate fungicides and avoid moving between wet plants to reduce spread.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Use certified seed and consult local extension for late blight alerts and resistant varieties.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.remedy: Improve ventilation in greenhouses, remove infected leaves, and apply fungicides when necessary.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Avoid high humidity and ensure proper spacing and airflow.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.remedy: Remove lower infected leaves, practice crop rotation, and apply fungicides during wet conditions.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Avoid overhead watering and maintain good sanitation.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.remedy: Use appropriate miticides or biological controls (predatory mites). Spray with water to dislodge mites in small plantings.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Avoid plant stress (proper watering), and monitor early for mite infestations.

Tomato___Target_Spot.remedy: Remove infected tissues and apply fungicide treatments if disease is widespread.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Rotate crops and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.remedy: No chemical cure. Remove infected plants and control spread through sanitation. Disinfect tools and hands after handling infected plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use virus-free seed/seedlings and practice sanitation; control tobacco and other reservoir hosts.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.remedy: No cure; remove infected plants. Control the whitefly vector using insecticides or integrated pest management.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties, reflective mulches, and control whitefly populations early.
